source.title: Cross-Layer Interaction under Weight-Space Ablation: A Closed-Form Attention Jacobian Bound and a Test on a Real Pretrained Model

page_placements.theme: IOI components interact through synergy and redundancy
Dataset-average circuits incompletely describe individual prompts

record.tranche_reason: It tests IOI-circuit behavior in a different pretrained model using Wang et al.’s activation-patching search, but changes the recovery metric to the final-token selector and adds jointly zero-ablated circuit probes.
record.gate_note: The IOI section reports activation-patching recovery, circuit overlap, zero-ablation collapse, dissociation, and interaction results. The marker-task experiments and mathematical bounds are not IOI-circuit tests; the sentiment, temporal-order, and magnitude-comparator results are candidate-mechanism screening rather than findings about the claim.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, five IOI matched pairs), the study finds small IOI circuits by activation patching. It then shows that zero-ablating those same circuits leaves much of the IOI logit gap intact. Patching and ablation effect sizes also differ on every instance. This bears on V5: how complete a circuit looks depends on the intervention used. It does not identify head classes or roles, backup heads, or GPT-2's circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors frame the Qwen IOI result as a mixed check of their companion paper's predictions (collapse, dissociation, interaction), not as a test of the IOI circuit claims. They report a shared head across all five instances, with collapse partial on four and absent on Anna/Mike. Dissociation appears on all five, and interaction is measurable on three, all at cross-layer pairs outside the theorem's scope.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Wang et al.’s original greedy activation-patching search, but on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and with recovery restricted to the final-token selector rather than the full vocabulary. Adds joint zero-ablation probes; search depth is capped at 6 sites per instance.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary across the five lexical instances. The study also reports different effect sizes for cross-input patching recovery and same-circuit zero-ablation, and its search is capped at 6 sites per instance.

fits_no_version.finding: Greedy activation-patching circuits for five name-varied IOI pairs in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct share one head (L25H9) in all five and another (L19H6) in four. The other 16 sites are instance-specific.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI circuits found per prompt pair in other models share a small core but are largely instance-specific across name substitutions.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly zero-ablating the first head and MLP in a circuit gives non-additive effects (relative interaction 0.066–0.327) at cross-layer pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Component ablation effects within IOI circuits are non-additive across layers.

record.problems: One model and five lexical IOI instances; one search result plateaus at 0.673 recovery. Collapse is absent on one instance. Interaction applies only to three instances and none is in the same-block configuration; uncertainty intervals are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI outcome rows omitted. The marker-task decomposition and curvature experiments are not IOI-circuit results; the other candidate mechanisms are only reported as pre-registered screening.

untested.parts: GPT-2 small is not studied. The 26 heads, 7 classes and the faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria are not evaluated.
No ablation of name-mover heads and no test of backup-head takeover.
A circuit is found in Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, but no head classes or roles (duplicate-token, S-inhibition, name-mover) are identified. Sizes, checkpoints and reuse for other tasks are not examined.
Only one search method is used, with no comparison of circuit-finding methods or of the circuits they recover.
Name order, templates and number of names are not varied. The five instances differ only in the names used.
Mean or resample ablation, metric choices, and prompt-distribution averages are not tested. Each circuit comes from a single matched prompt pair.

record.verdict_notes: The paper says it applies Wang et al.'s original method unchanged. In fact it uses a greedy activation-patching search with zero-ablation, at the final-token logit difference, on single prompt pairs. That differs from Wang et al.'s path patching and mean ablation over a prompt distribution, so the recipe is not an exact replication. The model is instruction-tuned. The study is a single-author preprint with no uncertainty estimates. The marker-task experiments and the bounds are unrelated to IOI.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, not GPT-2 small, and does not test the 26-head, 7-class circuit or identify the stated head classes and roles.
It does not ablate main name-mover heads or test backup-head takeover.
It searches one other model for an IOI circuit but does not test whether the GPT-2 head classes and roles recur, or whether components are reused for other tasks, sizes, or checkpoints.
It does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics to establish method independence.

It reports variation across five lexical instances and compares activation-patching recovery with zero-ablation measures, but does not systematically vary ablation types or evaluation metrics across matched conditions.
It tests five IOI lexical instances, but does not explicitly vary name order, sentence templates, or the number of names.

relationships.reason: Circuits recovering at least 0.96 of the gap under patching leave 17–76% of it after zero-ablation (R6–R10). Patching and ablation effects differ by 0.22–0.85 on every instance (R11–R15). Circuit completeness thus depends on the intervention.
relationships.display_finding: Circuits recovered at least 0.96 of the gap through patching but left 17–76% after zero ablation, with intervention effects differing by 0.22–0.85 on every instance.

relation.reason: Its own patching and zero-ablation measurements bear directly on V5's evaluation sensitivity.

tranche.reason: The study reports intervention-dependent IOI circuit evaluations in a new setting: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct with five lexical matched pairs.

source_check.notes: The probes compare different intervention estimands and do not directly evaluate the original circuit completeness criterion. The abstract and conclusion suggest dissociation exceptions, but Table 1 and Section 7.1 explicitly report non-small dissociation on all five instances.

statements.correction: Anna/Mike: patching recovery 1.000; collapse ratio 0.761. Appendix A reports an accompanying research repository and lists circuit-search, probe and figure-generation scripts; public accessibility is not established by the supplied text.
statements.problem: The Anna/Mike values are correct, but the claim that this preprint reports no code contradicts Appendix A.

statements.correction: L25H9 occurs in five circuits; L19H6 occurs in four. The remaining 16 sites each occur in one to three circuits, mostly exactly one.
statements.problem: The recurrence counts are correct, but describing all other sites as instance-specific can imply that each is unique to one instance.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Five IOI instances; patching-versus-ablation measures and joint circuit ablation
reader_labels.reason: Patching and ablation have nonzero dissociation gaps on all five instances (R11–R15); circuit ablation yields partial collapse on four and no collapse on Anna/Mike (R6–R10), with cross-layer interaction measured on three instances and differing in magnitude (R16–R18). This supports the study’s qualified, evaluation-dependent account, not a general estimate of the original GPT-2 circuit.

reader_labels.reason: A shared head occurs in all five circuits, another in four, and patching recovery is at least 0.963 on four instances (R1–R4, R19–R20).
